newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Essar seen signing basic telephone licence.
newsitem.headline: India's Essar seen signing basic telephone licence.

text.p: India's Essar Commvision, a joint venture between India's Essar group and Bell Atlantic Corp, is expected to become the third company to sign a basic telephone licence, a senior government official said on Friday.
"We expect Essar Telecom to sign the Punjab licence in the near future. We have had discussions, and Essar say they are ready," Telecom Commission chairman A.V. Gokak told reporters.
As secretary of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Gokak is the highest ranking civil servant in the Communications Ministry.
Only two companies, Bharti Telenet and Reliance Telecom, out of eight short-listed companies have accepted basic telephone services licences.

Basic telephone licences were auctioned by the Indian government in 1995 as part of an economic liberalisation programme that began in 1991. One licence for each of 21 zones was offered to compete against DoT's existing network.

But the privatisation drive got caught in bureaucratic red tape and legal wrangles, with the government dragging its feet over clearances and shortlisted companies unwilling to pay extensive licence fees.
Gokak said that there would now be only one more round of negotiations between the government and short-listed companies, after which the government would expect all of them to accept the licences.
"We have given them enough incentives and opportunities to accept the licences. There has to be a finality to the process," he said.
He did not say what would happen to any company that did not accept a licence after the final round of talks.
Gokak said the government was in the process of appointing an expert body to see how the costs of international long distance calls could be brought down.
He added that any decision to lower international call rates in keeping with trends the world over would be purely a political one.
On the issue of the DoT being opposed to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), Gokak said that both bodies had a good working relationship.

He said the DoT was considering appealing to the Delhi High Court against TRAI's recent decision barring the DoT from encashing bank guarantees of two operators that have defaulted on the payment of licence fees instalments.
